solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Screen bride's attendant behind house

indicators.note: behind places the attendant after the house in the answer

parts.note: a house is a home
a page is a boy who attends a bride at a wedding

explanation.surface: A wedding party scene: a bridesmaid or page is hidden behind a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' looks like a verb meaning hide, but it is the definition: the screen a website first shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A home page is the main screen of a website, the one a browser opens first.

clue.text: Woman who's expecting?

parts.note: the surface suggests a pregnant woman; the woman meant expects to inherit a fortune

explanation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' usually means pregnant, but here it means awaiting an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: An heiress is a woman due to inherit property or wealth, so she is expecting a legacy.

clue.text: Carving name into flesh is deliberate

indicators.note: carving one thing into another cuts it in, so a letter is set inside
into says the name letter goes inside the word for flesh

parts.note: flesh is meat

explanation.surface: A tattooist or butcher cutting a name into flesh does it on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meant was intended, done on purpose, which is what deliberate describes.

clue.text: Bound to open hands in US resort

indicators.note: to open means to go into the middle and split the word for hands apart

parts.note: palms are the insides of the hands
a bound is a leap, a spring

explanation.surface: Someone jumps to open their hands while at an American resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like a past tense meaning tied or obliged; here it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm Springs is a desert resort city in California, famous for golf and celebrity homes.

clue.text: Frisk doctor entering prison

indicators.note: entering means the doctor goes inside the word for prison

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor arriving at a prison is searched by the guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisk' suggests a body search at the prison gate, but it is the verb meaning to leap about playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To frisk and to gambol are both to skip and caper playfully, like lambs in spring.

clue.text: Stops wedding announcement being read

indicators.note: banns are read out in church, so this word heard aloud gives the answer

parts.note: banns are the announcement in church of an intended marriage

explanation.surface: A wedding is halted while the announcement of it is being made.
explanation.walkthrough: In British churches the banns are read on three Sundays before a wedding, so anyone with an objection can speak up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something is to prohibit it, so bans are stops put on things, as a verb: forbids.

clue.text: Maintain period is normal

parts.note: to maintain a view is to aver it, assert it
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a certain stretch of time is perfectly ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Average describes what is usual or standard, as in an average day.

clue.text: For investment, one's raised for example euros initially

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: one is I, so one's (one is) is IS

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of euros

explanation.surface: Looks like a finance note about raising money in euros for an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' is the military sense: surrounding a town to blockade it. 'For' is part of the definition, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a town, in the military sense, is to besiege it, so a siege is an investment.

clue.text: Irishman I brought forward for a summary

indicators.note: brought forward means the letter I moves nearer the front of the name

parts.note: Niall is a typical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: An Irishman produces a summary, bringing himself forward.
explanation.definitionFit: In all means altogether, in total, used when summing things up.

clue.text: Friend shielding revolutionary hacker

indicators.note: shielding means the friend's word surrounds and protects the revolutionary

parts.note: a mate is a friend
Che Guevara is the classic revolutionary

explanation.surface: A friend protects a revolutionary computer hacker from the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacker' suggests a computer criminal; here it is a tool that hacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife used to hack through vegetation, so it is a hacker.

clue.text: Shrub found in bed on holiday

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Easter is a public holiday

explanation.surface: A shrub turns up in someone's bed while they are on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotoneaster is a garden shrub with small leaves and red berries.

clue.text: Swallow starts to execute acrobatic turn

indicators.note: starts to means take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A swallow, the bird, begins an acrobatic turn in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' suggests the bird, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow food is to eat it, taking it down the throat.

clue.text: Ask Hector to cook something for tea

indicators.note: to cook letters is to rework them, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks Hector to make something for afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcake is a crumbly cake or biscuit served with afternoon tea, often with strawberries.

clue.text: Notice about dog to tie up

indicators.note: about means the word for notice goes around the dog

parts.note: to notice is to see
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A sign about a dog tells the owner to tie it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something is to fasten it firmly, as one ties up a boat.

clue.text: Dogs, a number wearing coats regularly

indicators.note: wearing means the letters from coats are put on around the number like clothes
regularly takes every other letter of coats

parts.note: the odd letters of coats
nine is a number

explanation.surface: A number of dogs are wearing coats as a matter of routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Canines are members of the dog family, so they are dogs.

clue.text: Determined to be under canvas

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in a tent, camping

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is in tent, which is where someone under canvas is.
explanation.definitionFit: Being intent on a goal is being resolved to achieve it, while in tent describes a camper.

clue.text: Clay pit being worked over in no way unusual

indicators.note: letters being worked over are handled and reshaped, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clay pit being dug over is nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something typical is representative and ordinary, the opposite of unusual.

clue.text: Book is nothing after a couple of pints

indicators.note: after places the nothing letter at the end, following the measure

parts.note: a quart is two pints
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A book is worthless after a couple of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarto is a book size, made from sheets folded twice into four leaves.

clue.text: Use plan in touring Korea, for one

indicators.note: touring means moving about, so the letters of use plan and in move into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller uses a plan while touring Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: Korea is an example of a peninsula, land almost surrounded by sea.

clue.text: One with a penny debt might …

parts.note: read cryptically: someone who owes a penny, P for penny followed by a word for one who owes

explanation.surface: Someone owing a penny might do something, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as P-OWER: P for penny, and an ower is one who owes, which the clue's words cannot split cleanly into separate pieces. The ellipsis runs this clue into the next; 'might' is the noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or force, which is what power means.

clue.text: Message on tomb that brings a tear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Rest In Peace, inscribed on gravestones
second meaning: to make a tear

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sad epitaph that makes mourners cry; the tear is a split, not a teardrop.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters stand for Rest In Peace on a gravestone, and as a verb they mean to tear.

clue.text: … cause pure chaos with European currency

indicators.note: chaos is disorder, so the letters of pure are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, a debtor might cause chaos with European money.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India, Pakistan and several other countries.

clue.text: Gain medal for gallantry, initially relieving castle

parts.note: to gain is to win
the DSO, Distinguished Service Order, is a British military award for gallantry

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of relieving

explanation.surface: A soldier wins a medal for bravery while relieving a besieged castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor Castle, west of London, is a royal residence of the British monarch.

clue.text: Subject to choose, not the last

indicators.note: not the last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to choose is to pick

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pick a subject but not the final one.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject of a talk, essay or discussion.

clue.text: Fungus that damages iron

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fungal disease of plants
second meaning: the corrosion that eats away iron

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses share the reddish-brown colour that gives them the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust names both a plant disease caused by fungi and the iron oxide formed when iron corrodes.

clue.text: One may show press instruction at an opening

definitions.text: One may show press instruction at an opening

parts.words: One may show press instruction at an opening
parts.note: this thing by a front door often bears a label telling callers to press it

explanation.walkthrough: 'press' and 'opening' suggest journalism or a launch event; the opening is a door and the press is a push of a button.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorbell is the button beside a door that visitors push to announce themselves.
